title: Chapter 7. The Journey through the Eastern Country and the Entry into the Northern Country
html:
Praise of Virachandra and Nityananda; Virachandra sets out with the nadas and his companions to preach the Hari-nama; the procession through East Bengal; the miracle at Dhaka and the conversion of the yavana ruler (pp. 54–60)

[p. 54]

1Sri Vira, the hero, a rod of punishment to the wicked,
the hero who cleaves the unruly elephant.1

2The hero [who overcame] the fearsome elephant Kuvalaya […],
the hero who revealed the hidden [glory] of Sri Radhika.

3On the drops of nectar from Nityananda's two feet,
O greedy bee of the mind, fix your thoughts.2

4The abode of Chaitanya's rasa,
taking again the name Virachandra, appeared in the age of Kali.
All the fallen and wretched, however many — the dull, the blind and the rest —
he flooded with waves of bliss.

5How lovely is his form, a feast for the eyes — like Kama embodied,
he glows with a crimson hue.
Calm, self-controlled, merciful, the wealth and life of the devotees,
ever in love with the rasa of Hari.

6There never was and never will be another like him: the Lord, descending,
came again and rose like the sun.3

7Who else in the three worlds can ward off the punishment of Kali —
he whose valour surpasses a lion's?
Says Vrindavana Dasa: the hope of my heart was not fulfilled;
deprived I remained, in confusion of mind.

8Glory, glory to Nityananda, the shelter of the world,
by whose mere will creation, preservation and dissolution take place!

[p. 55]

9He is called the original god, the eternal Brahman;
he is Chaitanya's elder brother, the treasure of Chaitanya's life.

10No one is dearer to Chaitanya than he;
ceaselessly [Chaitanya] dwells and sports in that body.

11Friendship, servitude, parental love and conjugal love —
apart from Nityananda, no one else has all of these.

12Who can know the greatness of such a Nityananda?
Only he knows him to whom Chaitanya reveals it.

13Nityananda-Balarama is the maker and the upholder;4
in the form of Sankarshana he dwells in the realm of Paravyoma.

14Through his portion he carries out creation and the rest,
and therefore Nityananda is the shelter of all.

15In his own form, becoming Govinda's elder brother,
he sports with Krishna together with their friends.

16In the form of a beloved dear as life he takes his pleasure with Krishna
and in the groves performs many pastimes, the rasa dance and others.5

17Who can understand these pastimes full of rasa?
No one but the intimate devotees has the right to them.

18Certain sinners of petty mind
make a distinction between Krishna and Rama — and are ruined, reduced to dust.

19The Lord's pastimes and qualities are beyond the reach even of the Vedas;
not understanding this, the sinner destroys himself by his talk.

20About that body in which Krishnachandra sports,
about its pastimes, the worthless sinner raises crooked arguments.

21What does the sinner think, even after looking into the scriptures?
Who can fathom Chaitanya's maya?

22Boundless is the greatness of him who is the origin even of Ananta;
what can I, a tiny soul, know of its limits?

23Relying on this strength — the nectar of Chaitanya's lips6 —
I cannot tell what I mean to say and what I am saying.

24My mind is maddened by the rasa of Nityananda's qualities;
whatever Chaitanya inspires, that I write down.

25May the devotees not count this as an offence;
may my mind ever rest at the feet of Nitai.

26My mind is captivated by the nectar of Nityananda's pastimes;
for my own fulfilment I taste a single drop.

27This is a most hidden account, endless and fathomless;
taste, then, the nectar of Virachandra's pastimes.

28Together with the devotees the Gosvami7 reflected:
"In the age of Kali the Lord revealed the Hari-nama.

[p. 56]

29The treasure of the Hari-nama is the essence of the essence of the four Vedas;
Sri Krishna Chaitanya proclaimed it.

30The nine kinds of bhakti and the extract of rasa
he revealed after a long interval.

31In the Lord's presence everyone accepts dharma;
but when his time has passed, they begin to do what is wrong.

32The Lord left me behind to keep [all] in check,
giving me the great Vaishnavas as my generals.

33I shall go round and survey the whole world;
where I see bhakti transgressed, I shall punish.

34Revealing four arms, I shall take the chakra in my hand
and punish whoever will not accept bhakti.8

35If the one who won the land does not watch over it,
everyone does as he pleases, and in time all is ruined.

36Inspiring fear and bhakti, I shall travel about."
Saying this, he resolved to set out on the road.

37With him were many great [Vaishnavas] and many disciples;
palanquins and horses were made ready.

38Beautiful were the banners — white, yellow, red and black;
some bore a full moon, others a half moon.

39A host of banners flew in the vault of the sky;
in the auspicious kirtan the nadas began to dance.9

40The cry rang out, "Hari, Hari!" and "Vira, Vira!" —
a sound that pierced heaven, earth and the netherworld.

41The world of the gods, the world of men, the world of the nagas —
all in wonder cried, "Hari, Hari!"

42With matchless splendour he took his servants along;
many fortunate ones came carrying the palanquins.

43Many servants held bunches of peacock feathers in their hands
and fanned him on all sides with white and black chamaras.

44Everyone was repeating the name of Krishna;
the cry "Hari, Hari!" pierced the three worlds.

45Trumpets and kettledrums boomed;
with the cry "Vira, Vira!" all the nadas made ready.

46In their hands were staffs of gold and silver, canes and flutes;
gunja garlands swung at their necks, red caps were on their heads.10

47Brimming with love for Krishna, they gave loud roars —
such prema he had placed in the bodies of them all.

48By the merciful glance of Prabhu Virachandra
all, filled with prema, went along with the Lord.

49Glory, glory to Mahaprabhu Virachandra Raya,
who floods the world with love [for the name] "Krishna Chaitanya"!

50In the form of Gaurachandra he revealed the mood of Vraja
and gave away the name of Krishna, filling the world with it.

51In the form of Virachandra he revealed this:
"Worship Gaura, say 'Gaura', become servants of Gaura!"

52Filling the heart with Nityananda's lotus feet,
keeping within the rasa of Radha and Krishna's prema —

53all this Prabhu Vira Raya made [people] take up;
with the company of devotees the Lord went on, performing his pastimes.

54Robed, the Lord rode in a palanquin;
[a turban on his head,] elephant-pearls swinging at his ears.11

55On the palanquin, inlaid with gold and silver,
a moonlike radiance shimmered.

56On his crimson body was the finest cloth;
on his lovely moonlike face, a gentle smile.

57All the nadas, intoxicated with prema, in a long file
went ahead at a swift pace, singing kirtan.

58The nadas danced like maddened lions;
their kirtan was only "Hari bol! Hari bol!"

59Mridangas, mandiras, dampas and kartals together;
on all sides the bees of his feet surrounded him.12

[p. 57]

60Jnanadasa, Krishnadasa, Ramadasa,
Nityananda Dasa and Ramai went surrounding the palanquin.13

61Nrisimha Dasa was the chief of all the nadas;
all the khandi-bearers14 went in front.

62All the companions with the Lord were full of prema;
whoever takes shelter of them is rid of the disease of worldly existence.

63Displaying the three gunas — sattva, rajas and tamas —
he won each over by what suited him, and went on, swaying in his palanquin.

64By learning [and austerity] heretics and pandits are won over;15
thus he made his conquest of the Eastern country.

65Seeing the power of Mahaprabhu and the power of his servants,
everyone said, "He seems to be the Lord himself!"

66From village to village there were festivals and the spreading of kirtan;
all who saw it were amazed.

67By the sankirtana of the Hari-nama the land was blessed;
he made famous the names of Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda.

68Giving the great mantra of the Hari-nama to living beings,
he himself sang and made the whole world sing.

69All became Vaishnavas, taking up the name of Krishna,
and cried, "Sri Krishna Chaitanya! Nityananda-Rama!"

70On all sides the host of devotees sang the qualities of Hari,
and in the middle danced Mahaprabhu Virachandra.

71While he danced, the Lord's own shakti shone forth;
for a krosha around there spread and sounded […].16

72Some saw that the Lord had four arms:
with two he clapped, two were raised on high.

73Everyone saw the Lord in many colours —
white, dark, crimson — with six arms.

74On all sides were heard the sounds of vina and flute,
the jingling of bangles, bracelets, anklets and belt-bells.

75Some saw Haladhara, some Vamshidhara,
some an avadhuta with a staff and a kamandalu in his hands.17

76Thus, revealing himself from village to village,
he gave the people prema-bhakti and fulfilled their lives.

[p. 58]

77In this way, swaying in his palanquin, he went into the Eastern country
and entered the capital called Dhaka.

78The ruler of that land was a yavana;
the Lord resolved, "I shall deliver him."

79He said to Nrisimha Dasa, "Go ahead of us;
take the khandi and go before the ruler.

80Tell him: a Gosai has come, a man of Gauda;
he will come to you, revealing the kirtan."

81Taking the order on his head, the chief of the servants
took the khandi, and the four of them set off.

82In front went Nrisimha Dasa, fearless at heart;
coming before the ruler, he spoke at once:

83"The Gosai of Gauda, out of mercy to you,
has sent his command: come out quickly to meet him."

84Saying this, he planted the standard in the courtyard;
seeing it, the courtiers were almost struck dumb.

85Hearing this, the ruler laughed and said, "[…]
Pull up the Hindu's staff and throw it outside!"18

86At the order, four [servants] took hold of the four khandis
and pulled with all their strength.

87They could neither let go nor lift them;
they stood like statues and could not utter a word.

88Then eight were brought, and they took hold again —
and it went the same with them, they were almost dead.

89Hundreds upon hundreds of strong yavanas were brought;
they came and seized [the poles] with great arrogance.

90As soon as they touched them, all their hands stuck fast,
and many more of the wicked ran away from afar.

91Then Mahaprabhu Virachandra worked his maya:
a fire blazed up seven palm-trees high.19

92Some burned in it and died, others shivered with cold;
and all the nadas leapt over the wall in a single bound.

93Going some way off, they sat on a high tower20
and, for sport, all of them urinated.

94They let loose their urine in torrents;
with a mighty roar the city was swept away.

95The flood rushed through the squares of the city of Dhaka
and then burst into the ruler's house.

96Houses fell, gates fell, mansions fell;
crying, "Save us, save us!" the townspeople were dying.

97The ruler sat stunned on his high throne
and thought to himself, "This is a buzurg Gosai."21

98The ruler said, "Where does this water come from without clouds,
flowing like this? Go and see, and bring me word."

99Just then news arrived there:
"The city is being swept away by the urine of the fakirs."

100Hearing this, the ruler was amazed
and in the yavana tongue began to call on Narayana.22

101The women of the inner apartments ran out in a panic,
crying, "We are drowning, we are drowning!" and wailing, "Alas, alas!"

102Running out in haste, they said these words:
"Where has so much water suddenly come from?"

103The wise dewan said, "This is the Gosai's wrath;23
take care, or worse will follow."

104In a panic the ruler went on foot,
repeating, "Gosai, save me!"

105With a straw tied at his neck24 and palms joined,
he came and fell before Nrisimha Dasa:

106"Save, save this fool — you are a living pir!25
Be merciful, Gosai — what hymns of praise do I know?

107Where is your Gosai? Show him to me;
seeing me, a low mleccha, have mercy on me.

[p. 59]

108As I showed contempt out of arrogance,
so I have received all the punishment I deserved.

109Some life is still left in me — forgive my offence,
take pity and show me favour."

110Hearing this, Nrisimha Dasa was filled with compassion;
he reassured him and freed him from fear.

111Seeing his humility, Nrisimha Dasa said:
"Do not worry, Krishna has shown you mercy.

112Come with me, saying 'Hari, Hari';
hearing it, the Lord will look on you with a merciful glance.

113The name of Krishna is dear to Prabhu Virachandra Raya;
whoever sings of Krishna, he forgives all his offences.

114Giving up your pride, you will lie prostrate at a distance,
and I, clasping his feet, will win you his mercy."

115The Lord had finished his bath and was [sitting there];
from afar that mleccha beheld him.

116[He saw him] beautiful and dark, in yellow garments, with eight arms:
in four hands the conch, discus, mace and lotus;

117in two hands he saw the Lord holding the great [bow] Gandiva and arrows,26
and with two hands, counting on his fingers, he chanted the name of Krishna.

118He saw his companions bearing mighty weapons,
with garlands reaching to the knees on everyone's neck.

119All were saying, "Krishna, Krishna! Hari, Rama, Rama!"
Their matchless radiance outshone millions of moons and suns.

120He saw his own pirs beneath [the Lord's] feet:
abandoning their own scripture, all were saying, "Krishna, Krishna!"

121In amazement the ruler spoke what was in his heart:
"This truly is the Gosai — there is no doubt of it.

122There was great pride in my mind
that my pir was higher than the Hindus' pir.

123So my scripture, the Koran, says,
but now with my own eyes I see that everything is otherwise.

124My pirs roll by the hundred at his feet!"
Seeing this, the mleccha ruler was astonished.

125"The Hindus' pir is the highest, the Lord of all" —
so the mleccha ruler thought to himself.

126Seeing Nrisimha Dasa, the Lord smiled and said,
"Tell me, who is this?"

127He replied, "Prabhu, this is the ruler of the land;
show him mercy, let his evil-mindedness depart.

128He has committed an offence against the Lord;
forgive him everything, Prabhu, and show him favour."

129Smiling, the Lord cast an auspicious glance on him;
the ruler fell prostrate and joined his palms.

130Casting off his own nature, the ruler made his plea:
"Such is the power even of a servant!

131Now it is plain to me27 that you are the Gosai:
everything is yours; for you there is no 'mine' and 'another's'.

132You are the true pir — I have seen it with my own eyes;
besides you there is no other in the world.

133You are the lord of the world, having taken a human form;
you cast an auspicious glance on the fallen and wretched.

134Deliver all the fallen in this world;
all beings are yours, you are the refuge of all.

135You have accepted even so vile a mleccha as me;
no power but the Lord's could do this.

136I deserve punishment, but show me mercy:
come to my city, let everyone see your feet."

137Saying this, he led the Lord to his own city;
a fine dwelling [for him] was the house of a brahmin.

138There was a new, lofty mansion, and on top of it
they spread a splendid couch for him to sit on.28

[p. 60]

139There [the Lord] made his ceremonial entry with his companions;29
the ruler with his people stood [before him].

140For darshan a dense crowd of people gathered;
staying on a high place, the Lord gave darshan.

141The Lord's body was lovelier than millions of Kandarpas;
the name "Hare Krishna" was ceaselessly on the Lord's tongue.

142Whoever saw him cried, "Krishna, Krishna, Hari!"
Thus he showed mercy to the high and to the middling.

143Hindus and yavanas alike all sang the name of Krishna:
such is Prabhu Virachandra, with a compassionate heart.

144Taking Nrisimha Dasa with him, the ruler went to his house
and surrendered himself completely.

145"I am of low birth, I have no rights at all;
but I have heard that [the Gosai] is the lord of everyone.

146In every reckoning the yavanas too are counted:
so say both my Koran and your Puranas."

147Saying this, he set costly cloths and jewels
on a worthy tray and presented them to him.

148Nrisimha Dasa pulled up the khandi and set off,
and coming before the Lord he told him everything.

149Receiving the cloths and jewels, the Lord laughed:
"Here is one of the Lord's wondrous pastimes!"

150Coming again, the ruler saluted the Lord with a kurnish.30
The Lord said, "Together with your people, say 'Krishna, Krishna!'"

151Hearing it from the Lord's lips, they said, "Krishna, Krishna, Rama!"
The Lord said, "You have attained liberation, fortunate ones!"

152Thus the Lord showed mercy to the yavana
and moved on with his companions, crying, "Hari, Hari!"

153In this way, having subdued Bengal,
he blessed the North by giving prema-bhakti.

154Whoever relied on learning, [austerity,] bhakti or power,31
admitting defeat in that, began to worship the Lord.

155Giving the names of Nityananda and Sri Krishna Chaitanya,
revealing the power of their pastimes and qualities,

156teaching the worship of Radha and Krishna,
proclaiming the dharma of the sankirtana of Krishna's name:

157"In the age of Kali there is no dharma but the name of Krishna;
singing Krishna's qualities, you will attain liberation without effort" —

158thus the Lord, giving the name of Krishna and bhakti,
delivered the Eastern and the Northern countries.

159Who knows the greatness of such a Prabhu Virachandra?
Sinners and the base take all this to be false:

160"What incarnation of Krishna in the age of Kali?
Which scripture says that Krishna sports in Kali?

161We know only the Kalki avatara at the end of Kali;
what incarnation of Krishna — all these are lying words.

162All these sinners do it to fill their bellies;
false plays and songs — nothing but deception."32

163All these heretics Virachandra Raya,
infusing them with shakti, made every one of them say "Govinda".

164Thus all the slanderers and heretics there were
he made weep, crying, "Nityananda! Sri Chaitanya!"

165All who listen with faith to these accounts
attain Sri Krishna Chaitanya.

166Hoping for the feet of Mahaprabhu Virachandra,
Sri Vrindavana Dasa tells the Vamsha-vistara.

Thus ends the seventh chapter of the Vamsha-vistara of Sri Nityananda Prabhu, in the Madhya-lila, called "The Journey through the Eastern Country and the Entry into the Northern Country".

Notes

  1. Couplets 1–2 are in short lines and badly corrupted in both copies. Khandi (khaṇḍi) here probably means "cleaving"; below, the same word denotes the banner-poles of Virachandra's companions. Kuvalaya (Kuvalayapida) is the elephant Krishna killed at the gate of Mathura; the beginning of line 2 ("ghoraddhi majjana") cannot be restored.
  2. The copies have "añje / adhe"; read as "ahe", "O!".
  3. Couplets 4–7 are tripadi. Stanza 6 survives only as a half-stanza: its rhyming partner (in "-ẏa") is missing in both copies; the end of stanza 7 rhymes only partly with that of 6.
  4. The copies have "kartā bhaktā"; read as "kartā bhartā", "maker and upholder".
  5. An allusion to the idea of Nityananda-Balarama as Ananga Manjari (see the end of ch. 6).
  6. According to tradition, Vrindavana Dasa's mother Narayani received Chaitanya's food remnants as a child; the author regards this as the source of his strength.
  7. The Gosvami here is Virachandra.
  8. Virachandra speaks as Vishnu bearing the chakra; the point is the protection of bhakti rather than literal slaughter.
  9. The nadas (nāṛaā, "shaven-headed ones") are Virachandra's followers; tradition holds that they were former Buddhist monks whom he received into Vaishnavism.
  10. Gunja: red-and-black seeds strung into necklaces; "ṭopa" is a headdress or cap.
  11. The copies have "śiṭhete vaiṭhala", which is unclear; restored from the sense.
  12. "The bees of his feet" are the devotees who cling to his feet.
  13. The first name is "jñatānadāsa" (Jnanadasa) in copy A and "prānadāla" (Pranadasa) in copy B; the former is adopted.
  14. Khandi (khaṇḍi): the banner-pole (below called nishan, standard) carried by Virachandra's companions.
  15. The opening of the line ("vidyāsādhyāẏa") is unclear; cf. couplet 154.
  16. The end of the couplet is corrupt in both copies ("vyāpita tura chaṭā vāje"); perhaps the sound of horns is meant. A krosha is a measure of distance, about 3 km.
  17. Haladhara ("bearer of the plough") is Balarama; Vamshidhara ("bearer of the flute") is Krishna; the avadhuta with staff and kamandalu is Nityananda's form.
  18. The ruler's speech apparently renders Hindustani; the word "junanikāpa" cannot be restored. "āśā" means a staff.
  19. Saptatala: as high as seven palm-trees.
  20. Tungi (ṭuṅgi): a raised hut or watchtower.
  21. Buzurg (Persian): "great", a saint.
  22. That is, he called on God in his own language.
  23. The copies have "egajapa / ejapa"; read as "e gajava", "this is the wrath" (Arabic-Persian ghazab).
  24. The copies have "kuṭāra"; read as "kuṭā", a straw — a sign of utter submission (cf. "a straw between the teeth").
  25. Zinda pir: "a living saint" (Persian).
  26. Gandiva is Arjuna's bow.
  27. "māluma": "plain, evident" (Arabic-Persian).
  28. "navaharmya" and "vasivāra" are restored from "navaharmadvara / navahargadarara" and "vivāra".
  29. Both copies read "caitanya vijaẏa"; translated according to the sense.
  30. Kurnish: a Muslim court salutation.
  31. The copies have "vidyā-mādhyā / vidyā-sādhyā"; sadhya is taken as austerity.
  32. Couplets 160–162 are the words of the slanderers.
